## Definitions

- [statement] The same short-horizon study warns that its 183-pair panel is not 183 independent replications: it reports mean pairwise correlation of 0.40 and an effective count near 2.5. It also states that the original pairs were ranked by volume measured after the sample ended, leaving survivor-tilted membership. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888
- [statement] Fidelity’s performance help says a withdrawal is not treated as a decline in return, while reducing the basis used for its return calculation; its money-weighted method still accounts for withdrawal size and timing. This is a product-specific accounting explanation; the same help text retains withdrawal size and timing in the money-weighted return calculation. (low confidence) — https://www.fidelity.com/webcontent/ap002390-mlo-content/19.09/help/learn_performancereporting.shtml

## Structure and components

- [statement] The author page explicitly describes the value-weighted and equal-weighted bias estimates as estimates for buy-and-hold portfolios. The weighting scheme is part of the reported result. (low confidence) — https://www.sebastianstoeckl.com/publications/wp2022_liebi_survivorship/
- [statement] Bull Bitcoin reports a historical comparison from January 1, 2016 to May 13, 2025 using weekly and monthly DCA with a minimum one-year holding period. It reports that DCA outperformed lump sum about 17.5% of the time in its analyzed portfolios, with smoother but lower gains. The post identifies market peaks followed by declines as cases where DCA can outperform in its sample. This is the vendor's reported historical result, not a forecast. The dates, frequencies and holding rule are part of its applicability. (low confidence) — https://www.bullbitcoin.com/blog/smash-buy-versus-dca
- [statement] Within its firm-reporting scope, the GIPS handbook combines returns on portfolio cash and cash equivalents with returns on the other portfolio assets. It treats allocation to cash as part of strategy implementation and includes cash performance when the firm controls the cash allocation even if it does not choose the specific cash vehicle. As a methodological application, an already funded reserve inside a bot’s measured portfolio should remain in that portfolio’s performance record during idle periods. (low confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/
- [statement] IBKR’s combined-component procedure first aggregates daily market values and flows across components, calculates a combined daily return, then geometrically links those daily returns. It states that adding component returns over the period does not produce the combined portfolio return. This is a useful accounting constraint when a study combines several bot sleeves or reserve accounts under one boundary. (low confidence) — https://www.ibkrguides.com/portfolioanalyst/money-weighted-return-white-paper-au.pdf
- [statement] For a proposed scheduled-DCA, grid or averaging-down comparison, report the funding boundary and reserve treatment alongside the return definition. TWR seeks to neutralize external flows, while the cash allocation already inside a portfolio remains part of strategy performance; MWR also reflects investor funding timing. Reporting these perspectives together is a methodological application of the distinction between external funding and cash already allocated within the portfolio. (medium confidence) — https://www.gipsstandards.org/standards/gips-standards-for-firms/gips-standards-handbook-for-firms/ · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.fidelity.com/webcontent/ap002390-mlo-content/19.09/help/learn_performancereporting.shtml
- [statement] Bailey and coauthors state that their PBO procedure does not check whether a backtest has correct transaction costs or uses only data available at the decision time. They also warn that it can miss overfitting to a regime when the available dataset contains no structural break outside that regime. (low confidence) — https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf
- [statement] In their 32-series portfolio example, Chekhlov, Uryasev and Zabarankin explain that randomly shuffling individual daily returns destroys autocorrelation. They instead use blocks of returns and the same block starting points across series to preserve the cross-market correlation structure. Their example does not supply a universal block length for crypto bot equity. (low confidence) — https://www.math.columbia.edu/~chekhlov/ChekhlovUryasevZabarankin--03-2004.pdf

## How it works

- [statement] The cited bot setup guide says Amount per trade applies separately to each selected pair and warns that simultaneous deals can cause insufficient balance. Its Summary-box documentation says bots and pairs compete for the same available funds, so their full requirements must be added. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] Bitsgap says a price-step DCA ladder struggles when price grinds downward without a meaningful bounce, because every safety order can fill and the ladder runs out. Block Research describes the same path as locking capital in unrealized drawdown after the last safety order. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The term Amount per trade has different meanings in the cited vendor guides: the cited bot setup guide defines it as the initial position size, while Cornix defines Amount Per Trade as the total potential amount assigned to a complete DCA cycle. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/
- [statement] Cornix states that Stop Loss Timeout can delay closure after the stop price is reached. It separately documents a continuous-stop count to deactivate the bot, a cooldown after trade close, and a total-cycle count before manual reactivation. (low confidence) — https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/
- [statement] OKX distinguishes nominal leverage from effective leverage: increasing position value without increasing margin raises effective leverage even if the nominal setting stays fixed. Its estimated-liquidation calculation assumes orders fill sequentially and stops if the liquidation price rises above the next execution price, so that estimate does not assume the bot can always reach every remaining safety order. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated
- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ gives a fee-adjusted geometric profit-per-grid formula and warns when profit per grid may not cover trading fees. The Dynamic Grid Trading paper uses a transaction fee of 0.0008 and reports lower profits from small grid sizes because fees consume a larger share of arbitrage profit; it also attributes poor IRR at large grid settings to infrequent activation. These are venue- and study-specific assumptions and findings. (medium confidence) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1
- [statement] Bybit's spot-grid documentation distinguishes realized Grid Profit from Total P&L, which includes unrealized changes in the held base token. It explicitly states that Grid Profit can remain positive while Total P&L is negative when inventory losses exceed realized profits. (medium confidence) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-trading-bot/spot-grid-bot-market-conditions
- [statement] Lipton and Lopez de Prado's abstract models oscillation using an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process and describes exits at a profit target, a maximum tolerated loss or a maximum holding horizon. It develops an analytical framework for profit-taking and stop-out levels by maximizing Sharpe ratio in that model. Leung and Li's abstract separately includes a stop-loss constraint in optimal entry and exit analysis. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.10502 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.5062
- [statement] With the same cash amount invested at each interval, scheduled DCA buys more units when price is lower and fewer units when price is higher. (medium confidence) — https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/dollar-cost-averaging · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/dollar-cost-averaging
- [statement] When the full investment amount is already available, spreading investment over time retains some cash and can forgo gains from immediate investment. FINRA and Vanguard describe this as an opportunity cost. (medium confidence) — https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/dollar-cost-averaging · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://corporate.vanguard.com/content/dam/corp/research/pdf/cost_averaging_invest_now_or_temporarily_hold_your_cash.pdf
- [statement] FINRA warns that per-transaction commissions or fees can make scheduled DCA more expensive than lump-sum investment because DCA creates more transactions. (low confidence) — https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/dollar-cost-averaging

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Two Binance Square community posts give different profit-per-grid rules of thumb: one suggests roughly 0.4% after fees, while another recommends net return per grid between 0.5% and 2%. These are attributed recommendations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/383611508716720
- [statement] The Short-horizon mean reversion study reports significant directional reversal in 90% of 183 Binance pairs and a gross edge peaking near 1.3 bp per trade against a 5 bp benchmark round-trip cost. The reported experiment evaluates directional sign predictability, and its authors distinguish detectability from profitability at that benchmark cost. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888
- [statement] The Dynamic Grid Trading paper reports BTC and ETH backtests from January 2021 to July 2024 and attributes much of its reported peak 60–70% IRR performance to rising cryptocurrency prices. A Stevens Institute project separately reports that its machine-learning parameter variants did not outperform traditional grid methods. These are reported study results. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://fsc.stevens.edu/cryptocurrency-market-making-improving-grid-trading-strategies-in-bitcoin/
- [statement] Bybit's Spot Grid FAQ states that initialization fails when estimated fill price deviates more than 10% from current market price, with the investment credited back. It separately describes failed initialization when slippage on the initial market buy leaves insufficient arbitrage opportunity or insufficient quote token to place the required orders. This is a venue-specific initialization safeguard. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.bybit.com/en/help-center/article/FAQ-Spot-Grid-Bot
- [statement] The SSRN abstract and author page for Ammann, Burdorf, Liebi and Stöckl's Survivorship and Delisting Bias in Cryptocurrency Markets report a sample of 3,904 cryptocurrencies from 2014–2021 and estimated annualized bias of 0.93% for value-weighted portfolios and 62.19% for equal-weighted portfolios. The two pages describe the same study. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4287573 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.sebastianstoeckl.com/publications/wp2022_liebi_survivorship/
- [statement] Cong, Li, Tang and Yang's NBER working paper tests 29 exchanges using data from July to November 2019 and estimates wash trading averaged over 70% of reported volume on the unregulated exchanges in its sample. Separately, Coin Metrics describes a Trusted Exchange Framework that vets data quality before calculating market metrics and selecting index constituents. (medium confidence) — https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w30783/w30783.pdf · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://coinmetrics.substack.com/p/state-of-the-network-issue-257
- [statement] CoinMarketCap describes its Liquidity Score as simulated immediate buy and sell slippage over order sizes from about $100 to $200,000, with greater weight on $100–$10,000 orders. S&P Global separately evaluates market volume, bid-ask spread, depth and slippage, and its report table gives mean 1% total Binance depth of EUR 0.40 million for EUR-USDC, EUR 1.00 million for BTC-EUR and EUR 31.10 million for BTC-USDT. These figures describe that report's sample. (medium confidence) — https://support.coinmarketcap.com/hc/en-us/articles/360043836931-Liquidity-Score-Market-Pair-Exchange · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.spglobal.com/en/research-insights/special-reports/liquidity-demographics-for-crypto-asset-trading
- [statement] CoinMarketCap describes its Liquidity Score as a purely quantitative measure using exchange API order books or exchange submissions, refreshed every two hours subject to order-book data availability. S&P separately describes cumulative bid-side and ask-side depth for a specified date and reports few executable Kraken USDC-USD trades within 1% of the peg in its March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank crisis example; it says participants might have been more willing to buy larger orders at the 10% level. These are provider descriptions and report examples. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://support.coinmarketcap.com/hc/en-us/articles/360043836931-Liquidity-Score-Market-Pair-Exchange · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.spglobal.com/en/research-insights/special-reports/liquidity-demographics-for-crypto-asset-trading
- [statement] Wash-trading estimates in the reviewed sources depend on estimator and coverage. Cong, Li, Tang and Yang report over 70% for their main unregulated-exchange estimate, about 61% after exchange-characteristic controls, and 16.3 percent for an alternative Benford-based estimate; they explain that the Benford method misses some wash trading. Coin Metrics calls Trusted Volume a lower-bound estimate that excludes DEXes and uncovered centralized exchanges, and warns that calculating an overall fake-volume percentage can give misleading conclusions. (medium confidence) — https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w30783/w30783.pdf · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://coinmetrics.substack.com/p/state-of-the-network-issue-257
- [statement] Vanguard's illustrated historical comparison reports lump-sum outperformance in 68% of rolling one-year periods. That example compares immediate investment with three equal monthly investments, assumes an equity portfolio with no interest on uninvested cash, and uses MSCI World Index returns from 1976–2022. (low confidence) — https://corporate.vanguard.com/content/dam/corp/research/pdf/cost_averaging_invest_now_or_temporarily_hold_your_cash.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] After price falls beyond the deepest safety order, the cited Summary-box documentation says the bot has spent its safety orders, holds the position, and cannot improve the average with further safety orders. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] OKX states that a futures DCA position may be liquidated if its margin balance falls below maintenance margin and that this can lose the initial funds. Bitsgap also distinguishes futures DCA liquidation risk from its spot DCA description. (medium confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained
- [statement] The cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide says Max Open Positions limits the cumulative number of open strategies across DCA bots and ignores or cancels new trade signals until an existing strategy closes when that limit is reached. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide
- [statement] KuCoin warns that low liquidity can cause large slippage and a situation where a trader can buy but cannot sell. A Binance Square community guide similarly warns that thinly traded coins can gap through several grid lines at once. (medium confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127
- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ states that grid price differences cannot be below tick size and that each grid order must meet a minimum notional requirement. A Binance Square spot-grid guide separately notes that every grid line must meet the pair's minimum order size. These constraints depend on venue and product. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.binance.com/en-ZA/square/post/381822568342127
- [statement] Binance's Futures Grid FAQ includes realized profit, unrealized PnL and funding fees in total profit. A Binance Square futures-grid guide lists funding fees among contract-selection considerations and warns that leverage amplifies losses and can increase liquidation risk. These are futures-grid considerations. (medium confidence) — https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/f4c453bab89648beb722aa26634120c3 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.binance.com/en-UZ/square/post/376851658061357
- [statement] OKX's Spot Grid documentation states that Trailing Down can extend the lower grid boundary when price continues falling. Each extension requires additional main-account capital; if funds are insufficient, the grid does not extend further. Its risk description warns of over-accumulating during a long bear market. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-the-spot-grid-bot-and-how-to-use-it
- [statement] The abstract of the preprint Volatility Harvesting or Inventory Risk? reports positive average after-cost grid increments at three- and five-year horizons for Chinese equity ETFs relative to a static portfolio with the same initial exposure. It also reports limited historical signals and no stable out-of-sample spacing-selection advantage over fixed rules. These are abstract-reported results for equity ETFs. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7429819
- [statement] The HODL Strategy or Fantasy? abstract reports Monte Carlo simulations across 378 non-stablecoin crypto assets, net of trading fees and the opportunity cost of one-month Treasury bills. It reports a median excess return of -28.4 percent at a two-to-three-year horizon. Its separate prediction analysis reports economically negligible and unstable effects from endogenous predictors based on realized risk-return metrics. These are the paper's reported simulation and prediction results. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02029
- [statement] The same study's SSRN abstract reports that a survival-conditioned sample overestimates its size premium by 50%. After controlling for survivorship and delisting bias, the abstract reports no evidence of a positive relationship between average returns and one-week momentum, market beta or downside risk. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4287573
- [statement] Concretum's tutorial describes using CoinMarketCap's historical OHLCV endpoint to retrieve daily open, high, low, close, volume and market cap by numeric coin ID. It presents a download workflow including active and defunct projects and warns that full execution can exceed 20 hours because of rate limits. These are the tutorial's stated data fields and execution warning. (low confidence) — https://concretumgroup.com/building-a-survivorship-bias-free-crypto-dataset-with-coinmarketcap-api/
- [statement] Cong, Li, Tang and Yang limit their wash-trading transaction sample to BTC, ETH, XRP and LTC, and the paper treats cryptocurrency-USD and cryptocurrency-USDT pairs as the same. Those are explicit sample and quote-currency conventions of this study. (low confidence) — https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w30783/w30783.pdf
_8 more problems, failure modes and limitations units in llms-full.txt#problems-failure-modes-and-limitations_

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The cited bot setup guide allows take-profit to use either the initial order or the average position price. A basket target tied to average entry is therefore a configuration choice in that guide, rather than a universal property of every DCA bot. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation defines maximum price drop covered as the deviation of the final safety order. Its cumulative-step formula is deviation(k) = p x (c^k - 1) / (c - 1) when c differs from 1, and p x k when c equals 1. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation defines required capital as the base order plus every safety order. For a safety-order volume multiplier m that differs from 1, it gives Required = V0 + V1 x (m^n - 1) / (m - 1). (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] Bitsgap warns that weak liquidity and wide spreads can consume the small take-profit targets used by its DCA bot. This is a vendor description of execution risk, rather than independent evidence of a profitable coin-selection threshold. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained
- [statement] Bitsgap describes averaging down as lowering average entry while adding exposure during a continued decline, and says it does not protect against a market that keeps falling. Block Research explicitly calls buying more as price drops a mechanic rather than an edge. These are scoped descriptions and commentary, rather than a measured positive expected-return result for the ladder itself. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] KuCoin's spot-grid documentation prefers liquid pairs with two-sided price movement and explains that a one-sided market may keep buying or selling instead of completing repeated buy-low/sell-high cycles. Bitsgap likewise describes frequent swings within a range as suitable and persistent one-way movement as unsuitable. (high confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/grid-trading-strategy-explained-how-to-profit-in-any-market-in-2026
- [statement] KuCoin's guidance prefers high liquidity and high volatility, whereas HaasOnline describes moderate volatility as suitable and advises avoiding volatility spikes. Bybit describes the tradeoff: wider swings can complete more grid trades, but swings large enough to exit the range halt execution. These are attributed qualitative guidelines. (medium confidence) — https://www.kucoin.com/support/20916860273561 · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://haasonline.com/grid-trading-bot, https://www.bybit.com/en/learn/bybit-trading-bot/spot-grid-bot-market-conditions
- [statement] Passivbot documents unilateralness as the absolute ratio of the exponential mean of completed one-minute log returns to the square root of their exponential mean square. It calls this directionality rather than absolute move magnitude. The documentation says implementation tests establish semantics and disabled-feature parity rather than profitability, and recommends assessing drawdown, exposure, underwater time, missed recoveries, fees and returns rather than fill counts alone. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/enarjord/passivbot/master/docs/adaptive_entry_cooldown.md
- [statement] Concretum's dataset tutorial describes CoinMarketCap's numeric UCID as a persistent identifier rather than a ticker, including across branding changes or delistings. Gimmer separately warns that the same ticker need not identify the same asset or contract and recommends recording venue, base, quote, symbol and listing or removal history. (medium confidence) — https://concretumgroup.com/building-a-survivorship-bias-free-crypto-dataset-with-coinmarketcap-api/ · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://blog.gimmer.com/2026/09/01/crypto-backtest-survivorship-bias-point-in-time-universe/
- [statement] For a removed market, Gimmer recommends retaining it through its last eligible timestamp and explicitly stating how an open position is handled, rather than silently deleting that record from the historical test. (low confidence) — https://blog.gimmer.com/2026/09/01/crypto-backtest-survivorship-bias-point-in-time-universe/
- [statement] Gimmer explicitly advises against treating every delisted asset as a total loss: it distinguishes removal, rename, migration and data loss, and calls for verified market history and an explicit open-position rule rather than assigning zero value or a successful exit without evidence. (low confidence) — https://blog.gimmer.com/2026/09/01/crypto-backtest-survivorship-bias-point-in-time-universe/
_15 more comparisons and alternatives units in llms-full.txt#comparisons-and-alternatives_

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Bitsgap describes its price-step DCA bot as a base order followed by lower safety orders and a whole-position take-profit above the average entry. Block Research distinguishes this price-triggered averaging-down from time-based DCA at a fixed interval. (medium confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The cited Summary-box documentation recommends leaving available-balance headroom for fees, slippage and other bots. It states that its summary figures assume all safety orders fill and exclude fees and slippage. (low confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16666593-understanding-the-dca-bot-summary-box
- [statement] Bitsgap describes pullbacks followed by partial recoveries as the favorable path for its DCA bot. It says a straight upward move after the base order leaves only that small initial buy in the trade. (low confidence) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained
- [statement] OKX warns that a martingale strategy can increase spending rapidly after a few transactions, especially during a prolonged price decline, and that exiting after funds run out can produce high losses. (low confidence) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated
- [statement] Both the cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide and the Cornix settings guide allow a stop-loss baseline to use either the initial/first entry or the average entry. (medium confidence) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://cornix.io/dca-bot-settings/
- [statement] Bitsgap qualifies its platform profit-rate analysis as pooling real-money and demo bots and removing unfinished launches, small deposits and outliers; it also says the typical size of losses is not published. Separately, Block Research describes frequent small closed wins alongside a large unrealized open loss. These source-specific disclosures show why a closed-profit rate alone does not quantify whole-account losses or expected returns. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://bitsgap.com/blog/what-is-a-dca-bot-the-averaging-ladder-explained · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://blockresearch.ai/blog/dca-bot
- [statement] The cited the cited bot setup guide setup guide distinguishes Position averaging, which begins applying its order-size multiplier from the second extra order, from Order averaging, which applies it from the first extra order. It also distinguishes fixed coin amount from fixed quote-currency order value. A ladder capital calculation must identify which of these documented configurations it represents. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide
- [statement] OKX documents a configuration-specific exception to an assumed positive liquidation price: for a long Futures DCA position, an absent estimated liquidation price may mean its margin is sufficient that it would not liquidate even at a zero asset price. The documentation uses "may"; absence of the displayed price alone is not an unconditional safety guarantee. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated
- [statement] Stopping new activity need not release an existing position: the cited bot setup guide documents a Stop choice that leaves trades open and monitored, while OKX says pausing its Futures DCA bot cancels pending orders but retains the current position and keeps TP/SL active. These documented controls therefore require an explicit distinction between pausing new orders and closing inventory. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08) — https://help.3commas.io/en/articles/16281102-how-the-dca-bot-works-strategy-setup-guide · keywords: Crypto coin selection for grid and DCA strategies · also: https://www.okx.com/en-us/help/whats-futures-dca-bot-and-how-do-i-maximize-my-efficiency-with-automated
- [statement] The Dynamic Grid Trading paper concludes that its finite grid has zero expected value under its stated equal-probability up/down price-step model, with no transaction fees and liquidation below the lower grid boundary. This is a conditional model result. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11921v1
